notes.text: Ludwig van Beethoven, Bagatelle No. 25 in A minor, WoO 59 ('Für Elise'), c. 1810, published 1867. Public domain. A section only: the pickup and bars 1–22 of the standard text, the first repeat written out (first ending, then second), stopping before the F-major episode. 3/8 at 76 bpm: count the dotted quarter, one pulse per bar. Bar 1 here is the two-note pickup; bars 2–9 are the score's bars 1–8.

Starter song. Notes follow the Breitkopf & Härtel text; chord labels are the textbook readings. The left hand is one track of single notes (its broken chords are played one note at a time, never together).
Pickup: E–D#, a half step. The whole theme grows out of this pair.
The theme: E–D#–E–D#–E–B–D–C. The bass is silent under it — the chord arrives only when the melody lands on A in the next bar.

notes.note: i — the bass spells A–E–A, the melody answers with C–E–A
V in first inversion; the G# in the bass is the leading tone
i; the bar ends with the E–D# pickup again
V; the melody's C is a neighbor above B
i — first ending: A holds, then E–D# turns back to the top
i — second ending: B–C–D climbs into the next phrase instead

notes.text: Four bars, each a held note plus a three-note turn (E: G–F–E; D: F–E–D; C: E–D–C), stepping down E–D–C–B while the bass walks C–G–A–E.

notes.note: III — the relative major, touched for one bar
VII, or V of C: the bass has G–G–B
V, bare: E–E–E in the bass and B on top, no third — a half cadence

notes.text: Two bars of E and D# alone, with one leap up to E6: the pickup figure stretched out, with rests, before the theme returns.

notes.note: i — the A-minor cadence that closes the A section; the F-major episode would start here
